items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: he was on a Dick Hyman record that I just think is great

ctx.x: That Freddie Green rhythm. Well Bucky’s a master of that.

Yeah. And it’s also the notes he puts on top of the chord, too. I’ve noticed, in fact I wanted to talk about Milt Hinton a little, he was on a Dick Hyman record that I just think is great. And it wasn’t just the chunking, it was the note as it moved on the top of the chord [scats], you know that voice leading.

Well you know, I’ll tell you a little secret. Most of the time there’s one note in the chord. Most of the time Bucky’s doing, he’s dampening most of the notes and playing one, the third or the seventh [scats]. You listen carefully. There’s not six notes, five notes, there’s not even three notes. At best there’s two notes. Two notes coming through and the rest of it is chunk, chunk, chunk, chunk. And you get that sensational combination of a drum [scats]. He is the simplest guy. And that’s why he can play any song…
